title: Report a problem and track it to resolution
journey: The citizen captures a photo with location and timestamp at the shutter, the complaint is created with a ticket id, the office sees it live and assigns and resolves it with a proof photo, and the citizen confirms or rejects; a rejection reopens the complaint and silence auto-resolves it on a deadline.

steps.action: The citizen captures a photo through the in-app camera only (no gallery), with lat/lng and a timestamp taken at the shutter, plus a category and optional note.
steps.notes: Photo is compressed under 500 KB and uploaded to complaints/{complaintId}/photo.jpg; the doc is created with status = received, escalationLevel = 0, deviceId = auth uid.

steps.action: The complaint is created with a ticket id (PMH-YYYYMMDD-NNNN) and the citizen can watch its status in My Complaints.
steps.notes: listenToTicketUpdates reads the same doc in real time so the citizen sees status changes.

steps.action: The office sees the complaint live in the complaints table, assigns it to a staff member, and resolves it with a cleaning proof photo (resolvedPhotoUrl).
steps.notes: setComplaintStatus re-reads the live staff doc (instant revocation) and writes status = resolved with resolvedPhotoUrl and autoResolveDeadline.

steps.action: The citizen verifies the resolution: confirms (complaint stays resolved, deadline cleared) or rejects (status = reopened, complaint goes back to the office).
steps.notes: Cross-verification loop: confirmed true → resolved; confirmed false → reopened.

steps.action: If the citizen never answers, autoResolvePendingComplaints flips pending_verification to auto_resolved once the autoResolveDeadline passes; the citizen may still reopen it.
steps.notes: Scheduled server function, runs every hour; auto_resolved is not final.

steps.action: The driver may update the status of missed_collection complaints in its route's wards (Pending Reports: Will Revisit → assigned, Done → resolved with resolvedAt).
steps.notes: Direct Firestore write through FirestoreComplaintsRepository, scoped to the driver's route wards; not a callable.

slices.evidence: apps/citizen_app/src/services/firebaseService.ts syncComplaintToCloud creates the complaints doc with deviceId = auth uid and listenToTicketUpdates reads it in real time; apps/citizen_app/src/components/CrossVerifyModal.tsx and PostCollectionModal.tsx are the confirm/reject UI.
slices.blockedBy: The confirm/reject loop writes to localStorage via storageService, not to the citizenVerifyResolution / reopenComplaint callables, so the cross-verification loop is not wired end to end.

slices.evidence: src/App.tsx routes complaints to A17_Complaints; src/services/dataService.ts resolveComplaint / assignComplaint write localStorage under prefix safai_v3_.
slices.blockedBy: The admin panel has zero Firebase; its data layer is a pure localStorage mock, and it calls no callable.

slices.evidence: lib/core/repositories/firestore/firestore_complaints_repository.dart updateStatus writes complaint status and resolvedAt directly to Firestore; watched by watchMissedCollectionComplaints.

handoffs.notes: The citizen creates the complaint; the office sees it in its complaints table.
The office resolves with a proof photo; the citizen's app picks up the status change via its live read.
The citizen confirms or rejects; a rejection reopens the complaint for the office.

scenario.name: Complaint loop end-to-end (PRD-1 Test C1)
steps: Citizen submits a complaint with photo and location from the user phone.
The complaint appears in the admin panel complaints table with photo and location within 10 seconds.
The admin assigns and resolves it with a proof photo.
The citizen sees the status change and confirms or rejects.
A rejection reopens the complaint; silence auto-resolves it on the deadline.

openQuestions: The user app's stack is React/Vite, not Flutter as the PRD states.
The user app's firebase project id is hardcoded to safai-saathi-panchmahal while the platform project is safaaisaathi-63a87; confirm which project complaints target.
The citizen confirm/reject loop writes to localStorage, not to the citizenVerifyResolution / reopenComplaint callables; decide whether to wire the callables or keep local writes.
CHG-0011: the citizen app must not write wardDuty; the direct wardDuty write in firebaseService.syncWardDutyToCloud is a bug to remove.
